name: Median Graphs Are Strictly Contained in Convex-Geometry Ideals
scope: Finite one-inclusion graphs, up to signed-coordinate equivalence and suppression of constants.
statement: Every median graph is a convex-geometry ideal graph, and the inclusion is strict.
proof: The inclusion is the convex-geometry representation theorem for median graphs. For strictness, $Q_3^- = Q_3\setminus\{111\}$ becomes the upper ideal $Q_3\setminus\{000\}$ after complementing all coordinates, so it belongs to $\mathsf{Icg}$; it is not median because the majority of $110,101,011$ is the missing vertex.
